title: Use a trine to disprove a universal three-source balanced entropy lift
statement: The scalar balanced third finite difference of s(t)=-t log t is nonnegative, but three positive qubit trine projectors make the corresponding matrix trace-entropy expression strictly negative. The failure persists for sufficiently small faithful epsilon-identity perturbations.

requires: A proposed universal scalar-to-matrix lift for a balanced three-source entropy expression.
provides: An explicit 2x2 noncommuting obstruction showing that scalar validity of this balanced three-source inequality does not imply its matrix version.
assumptions: P_i are the three real qubit trine rank-one projectors; S(Y)=-TrYlogY and log is natural. Faithful persistence follows by continuity after P_i -> P_i+epsilon I.
costs: Exact 2x2 spectra and logarithmic evaluation, plus continuity; no channel or physical experiment is used.
contract.obstruction: Does not refute the two-source theorem, the W3 target, or a fixed-prior matrix-SDPI theorem; an SDPI separation needs a compatible channel and prior.

body: For positive a,b,c, the scalar third finite difference is the triple integral of s'''(u+v+w)=1/(u+v+w)^2 and is nonnegative; boundary cases follow by continuity. For the trine, sum_iP_i=(3/2)I, each pair has eigenvalues 3/2 and 1/2, and each singleton has eigenvalues 1 and 0. Evaluating S of those spectra gives 3/2 log(3/4)<0. Adding epsilon I to each P_i changes the expression continuously, so it remains negative for all sufficiently small positive epsilon. This is one explicit failure of a three-source scalar lift, not a W3 input or a channel-SDPI counterexample.
